title: Paragraphs
definition:
The `

` element represents a paragraph of text. Browsers automatically add an empty line (margin) before and after each `

` element.
simpleExplanation:
The bread and butter of text on the web. Any standard block of reading text should be wrapped in a `

` tag.
realWorldExample:
Writing a blog post. Every separate block of text is its own `

` tag.

basic:
Is the `

` tag a block-level or inline element?
intermediate:
What happens if you put a bunch of extra spaces and line breaks inside a `

` tag in your code?

answers.question: Block or inline?
answers.answer: Block-level. It always starts on a new line and takes up the full width.

answers.question: Extra spaces?
answers.answer:
Browsers ignore them! This is called 'whitespace collapse'. Even if you press 'Enter' 10 times inside a paragraph in your HTML file, the browser will render it as a single space. You must use the `
` tag to force a line break.

codeExample:
This is a standard paragraph. It automatically has some space above and below it.

This is a second paragraph. It sits below the first one.

If I press enter in my code... The browser totally ignores it! I can put 10 spaces, and it shrinks to one.

If you actually want a line break,
you must use the Break tag.

Now I have empty lines!
